title: Fingerstick a trainer hand: twist the lancet's tab off, hold the ring finger still, fire square, discard in sharps
instruction: A fingerstick trainer lies palm up: a palm block with an index finger, a thumb and a ring finger, rolled so the side of the ring fingertip faces up; the ring finger rides on a light spring and gives way when pressed unless it is held. A BD Microtainer contact-activated lancet (21 G x 1.8 mm) stands tip down in a stand whose socket holds its protective tab, and a BD sharps container stands beside. Do a fingerstick as BD directs. Done means: the lancet's tab was twisted off in the stand before the lancet came out of it; the ring finger was held still by a gripper closed on it from the lancet's first touch until after it fired; the lancet fired square to the skin on the side of the ring fingertip's pad that faces up, without sliding; the used lancet is inside the sharps container, let go; and the trainer's base was not moved.
context: O*NET Core tasks (relevant to at least 67% of incumbents): Phlebotomists 31-9097.00 (Employment (2025) 143,900), "Draw blood from capillaries by dermal puncture, such as heel or finger stick methods."; Medical Assistants 31-9092.00 (833,900), "Collect blood, tissue, or other laboratory specimens, log the specimens, and prepare them for testing." The CMA (AAMA) exam outline lists "Capillary/Dermal puncture (finger, heel, ear)"; NCCT's medical assistant plan, "Perform capillary punctures (i.e., fingerstick, heelstick)." BD's guide: "Twist off the tab"; "press safety lancet firmly against the puncture site." A hospital laboratory procedure for this lancet's family: "Grasp the finger, and using a sterile lancet, press firmly against the finger to make a puncture." The skill: one hand holds the punctured finger still while the other fires a sharp square on its curved tip.
setup: Coordinates: x forward from the arm bases (at y +-0.305), y left, z up from the table top. Fixed: a stand (40 mm square, 25 mm high, printed) at (0.27, -0.19): a fixed post holds the lancet's tab cap and a cup on it, keyed to the lancet's front (13.8 x 10.8 mm pocket, 8 mm deep), turns up to 100 deg either way; the tab breaks off when the lancet is turned 45 deg either way, against 3 N-cm (rig.scad, parts stand and cup). A BD 305635 sharps container (124.5 x 109.2 x 165.1 mm), centred at (0.14, -0.225), its lid opening 63.5 x 30.5 mm. Loose: a BD Microtainer contact-activated lancet 366577 (21 G x 1.8 mm, pink), modelled as a 13 x 10 x 37 mm polypropylene housing (4 g) and a 7 mm contact shield standing 3 mm proud on a spring (4 N/mm, 1 N preload); it fires at 8 N on the shield (1.75 mm of travel). It stands tip down in the cup. A fingerstick trainer (printed PETG, rig.scad) lies palm up on a 3 kg base plate taped down: a palm block with an index finger and a thumb, fixed, and a ring finger (life size, tip radius 7.3 mm, 25 g) on a vertical linear guide under its knuckle: two springs (0.1 N/mm in all) hold it up on a top stop with 1 N to spare over its weight, so a downward push of 1.20 N moves it 2 mm, and it stops 10 mm down. No middle or little finger. The hand is rolled 30 deg about its fingers so the side of the ring fingertip faces up; the ring's tip at (0.19, -0.005) and 77.3 mm over the table, the fingers pointing toward the wrist 30 deg right of +x (before the seed's shift). The base is shifted in x and in y each uniform within +-12 mm and turned uniform within +-6 deg about a point 130 mm behind the ring's tip along the hand (the palm's middle), drawn from the trial's seed.
scoring: The site: the side of the ring fingertip's pad that faces up, 8 to 15 mm back from the apex and 15 to 45 deg round from the pad's middle line; the shield's face within 1.5 mm of the skin is on it. Square: the lancet's axis within 10 deg of the skin's local normal where it touches. A slide: the face moving more than 1 mm on the skin between first touch (the shield pushed off its stop, 1.2 N) and firing; lifting off ends a placement. Held: a gripper closed on the ring finger, its finger half-gap 5.7 to 8.7 mm (within 1.5 mm of the 7.2 mm it reads closed on the finger), its TCP within 15 mm of the finger's axis between its distal joint and its base and at most 4 mm off the axis along its closing direction, its pad tips below the axis; it must hold at every step from the lancet's first touch until 0.5 s after the click. Still: the ring finger pushed at most 2 mm down, read at its slide and at its fingertip, over the same window. Out of the stand: the lancet moved more than 4 mm across or 10 mm up from where it stood; once out it stays out, so a lancet put back in the stand and let go is a drop. Rungs (0 once any fault has latched; 0.4 and 0.6 count once reached, the others are read at the last step): 0.2 the tab twisted off and the lancet out of the stand; 0.4 and the lancet has touched the site (contact: the shield off its stop), square, with the ring finger held and still; 0.6 and fired there, square, held, still, without a slide; 0.8 and the used lancet inside the sharps container, let go by both hands; 1.0 that held 1 s. Scored 0 from then on: the lancet lifted out with its tab on; the lancet fired in the stand (tab off, pressed down on the post); the ring finger not still; a step without the hold from first touch to 0.5 s after the click; a fire with no gripper holding the ring finger; a slide; a fire off the site or tilted; the lancet, once out of the stand, held by neither gripper and outside the container for 0.5 s (dropped; held: a gripper's finger half-gap 3 to 7 mm, so closed on either side of the housing, and its TCP within 15 mm of the lancet's axis from 10 mm beyond its face to 53 mm up it; let go: a gripper's half-gap over 7 mm or its TCP over 60 mm from that axis); the trainer's base dragged, lifted or pushed down 5 mm, or turned or tipped 2 deg; the lancet 30 mm under the table top; the firing model not running. Real trials (README) read the touch on a kitchen scale under the trainer (a change of 56 g, 0.55 N, a one-way bound on the sim's touch), the stillness on steel rules beside the web and the fingertip (side camera, 60 fps), the hold on the cameras and the arm's log, the click on audio.
reset_notes: A new lancet in the cup each trial (a used one is spent; its tab stays in the post's slot and is removed); the ring finger back on its top stop; the base placed by seed; the container emptied of the trial's lancet.
fidelity: Approximate. The lancet's drive is a sprung shield that fires at a set force; needle, puncture and blood are not simulated. The tab is a sprung turn that breaks at 45 deg either way; a pull-off is not modelled. A real finger's give at its joints, wrist and arm is one sprung slide at its knuckle; skin does not deform. The lancet's size, fire force, tab torque and the slide's spring are estimates, measured before trials; the held rule's on-finger half-gap (7.2 mm) is planned, checked on the film.
